title: 3785. Minimum Swaps to Avoid Forbidden Values

examples.explanation: One optimal set of swaps: Select indices i = 0 and j = 1 in nums and swap them, resulting in nums = [2, 1, 3]. After this swap, for every index i, nums[i] is not equal to forbidden[i].

One optimal set of swaps: Select indices i = 0 and j = 2 in nums and swap them, resulting in nums = [6, 6, 4, 5]. Select indices i = 1 and j = 3 in nums and swap them, resulting in nums = [6, 5, 4, 6]. After these swaps, for every index i, nums[i] is not equal to forbidden[i].
It is not possible to make nums[i] different from forbidden[i] for all indices.
No swaps are required because nums[i] is already different from forbidden[i] for all indices, so the answer is 0.

hints: Count combined frequencies of values in nums and forbidden into a map freq.
Collect bad positions (nums[i] == forbidden[i]) into a map badPairs[val] counts.
Let badPairsSum be the sum of all bad counts and maxBadPairs the maximum bad count for any single value.
The minimum swaps equals max((badPairsSum + 1) / 2, maxBadPairs) (i.e. ceil(badPairsSum/2) vs the largest same-value bad cluster).
